# Psalm 75 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** To the choirmaster: according to Do Not Destroy. A Psalm of Asaph. A Song. We give thanks to you, O God; we give thanks, for your name is near. We recount your wondrous deeds.

**2** "At the set time that I appoint I will judge with equity.

**3** When the earth totters, and all its inhabitants, it is I who keep steady its pillars. Selah

**4** I say to the boastful, 'Do not boast,' and to the wicked, 'Do not lift up your horn.

**5** Do not lift up your horn on high, or speak with haughty neck.'"

**6** For not from the east or from the west and not from the wilderness comes lifting up,

**7** but it is God who executes judgment, putting down one and lifting up another.

**8** For in the hand of the LORD there is a cup with foaming wine, well mixed, and he pours out from it, and all the wicked of the earth shall drain it down to the dregs.

**9** But I will declare it forever; I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.

**10** All the horns of the wicked I will cut off, but the horns of the righteous shall be lifted up.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 75.

- **75:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **75:4** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **75:6** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **75:8** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **75:10** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **75:3** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **75:2-5**: Direct divine speech in the psalm — YHWH himself speaks as cosmic judge; rare in the Psalter.
- **75:8**: The 'cup' of YHWH — yayin chamer ('wine foams') with mesekh ('mixture/spice') — an image of divine wrath poured out for the wicked.

### LOGOS
- **75:1**: 'Do Not Destroy' (al-tashcheth) appears also in Psalm 57-59 — possibly a tune name. The psalm is a thanksgiving that God will judge at the right time.
- **75:6-7**: The compass-point language (east, west, wilderness = south) conspicuously omits north — where Zion/God's throne is located. Exaltation comes from God alone.

### PNEUMA
- **75:2-3**: God's voice breaking into the psalm is electrifying. While the world is falling apart, God calmly says: 'I'm the one holding the pillars.' That's reassurance at a cosmic level.
- **75:8**: The cup of God's judgment is one of the Bible's most vivid images — foaming, spiced wine that the wicked must drink to the dregs. It shows up again in Revelation 14.

— SOPHIA
